definitions.unit: A task on the grid; a logged step for off-policy estimates.
definitions.success_rate: Mean success over units. Unlabelled outcomes are excluded from the headline and bounded in the 'unlabelled_sensitivity' diagnostic; they are never failures.
definitions.cost_per_task: Mean realized cost in USD per task, failures included.
definitions.cost_per_step: Mean realized cost in USD per logged step, failures included.
definitions.cost_per_solved: Total spend divided by units solved (mean cost / success rate), so failed attempts are paid for. Null when nothing is solved; an unbounded interval is flagged.
definitions.quality_retention: Success rate divided by that of the strongest single configuration (highest success, then cheapest) on the same units. Not capped: above 1 means the policy solves more than the strongest configuration.
definitions.strongest_solved_retained: Grid only: of the tasks the strongest configuration solves, the share the policy also solves (at most 1).
definitions.switches_per_task: Grid: expected model changes between cascade attempts within a task (0 for a single configuration).
definitions.config_changes_per_task: Grid: expected (model, effort) changes between attempts.
definitions.switch_rate_per_step: Logged: probability that the policy's first step uses a model other than the state's cache owner, averaged over logged states.
definitions.added_latency_p50_ms: Grid: median over tasks of the latency of cascade attempts before the one that produced the result (routing-decision time is not in the data). Null on logged data.
definitions.total_latency_p50_ms: Grid: median end-to-end latency of the policy's runs per task.
definitions.total_latency_p95_ms: Grid: 95th percentile end-to-end latency per task.
definitions.frontier_margin: Success rate minus the frontier's success rate at the policy's spend, in success-rate units. The frontier is the upper concave envelope of every single configuration's (spend, success) point and the origin.
definitions.cost_saving_at_equal_success: Grid: the frontier's least spend reaching the policy's success rate, minus the policy's spend (USD per task). Null and flagged when no configuration reaches it.
definitions.utility: success_rate - cost_weight * cost, only when a cost weight is given.
definitions.verdict: beats_frontier when the margin's interval lies above 0; does_not_beat when it lies at or below 0 (a tie does not beat); not_shown otherwise, or when the data cannot support a verdict (reasons listed).
definitions.interval: Percentile cluster bootstrap at the stated confidence: whole tasks (or sessions without a task id) are resampled, paired across policies and configurations.
definitions.ess: Kish effective sample size of the importance weights, (sum w)^2 / sum w^2.

evaluations.scope: Task-level, full-information evaluation on the replay grid. Each policy's decision at task start is applied to the whole task, as one configuration or a cascade of configurations. No run in the grid switches model within a task, so step-level routing, the switch tax and within-task switching are NOT measured here; they can only be estimated from logged traces with propensities.

frontier.definition: upper concave envelope of the single-configuration points and the origin (declining a unit); flat beyond the configuration with the highest success

notes: Cascades are simulated from independent single-configuration runs: a cascade succeeds if any step's run succeeded and pays for a step only when every earlier step failed. Each step's cost is that of a fresh run, so cache reuse between steps (and any benefit of seeing the earlier failure) is not in the data.
Added latency is the time spent in cascade attempts before the one that produced the final result; routing-decision time is not in the grid and is not included.
